key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implants must be designed as coupled biomechanical-biomaterial systems, where macro-geometry, graded Ti-HAp interfaces, and coating durability jointly determine load transfer and osseointegration.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that clinical translation of these implants depends on validated gait-phase finite element models, fatigue/coating-integrity testing, and biomaterial interfaces that can survive cyclic loading while supporting bone integration.
method: Systematic review of DWBI design, biomaterials, and clinical translation
Trend analysis of 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies
Synthesis of FEA, FGM/graded Ti-HAp, in-vivo osseointegration, and rehabilitation evidence
evidence_signal: The evidence base is still immature: more than half of the empirical studies were bench or simulation only, with animal and human/clinical validation forming a smaller layer.
watch_item: Graded Ti-HAp and FGM concepts are promising, but much of the support comes from non-DWBI analog studies, so device-specific validation under patient-realistic loading is still needed.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
